definition.given: On a Chatflow Studio page, a failed Publish Update attempt displays a validation toast above the Features and Publish controls; closing it starts a fade-out.
definition.when: The person dismisses the toast, immediately clicks its center during fade-out, then uses Features and Publish after the toast disappears.
definition.observed: The toast becomes visually absent but remains as a transparent dialog over the header, so subsequent clicks on Features and Publish are intercepted and neither control opens.
definition.require: Once the toast is visually absent, the underlying Features and Publish controls receive pointer input and remain operable.
allow: The toast may animate out, provided it relinquishes pointer input no later than the moment it becomes visually absent.

theory.title: Action lifecycle and immediate feedback
theory.rationale: Dismissing transient feedback is part of the action lifecycle. Once the toast appears gone, its interactive scope must end immediately; an invisible hit target makes visual feedback contradict actual actionability and blocks the next explicit command.

reference_observation: After the dismissed toast fades away, clicking Features opens its drawer and clicking Publish opens the publishing popup.
requirement_rationale: A validation toast is temporary feedback rather than a lock on Studio. Relinquishing its hit area when it disappears lets the user continue using the controls beneath it.
